blocks.text: Private Access (ZPA) only supports passive FTP mode; active mode is not supported.. Active FTP requires a TCP connection initiated from the server to the client, while passive FTP only requires client-initiated TCP connections. If an FTP client attempts active FTP mode or sends an active mode request in parallel to the passive request, the attempt fails.
To support FTP applications in passive mode:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Private Access > Private Applications > Defined Application Segments.

blocks.text: The Add Application Segment window appears.

blocks.item: In the Add Application Segment window, on the Define Applications page:
For Applications, enter an IP address. Private Access only supports IP-based passive FTP applications.
For Client Connector Access, add the TCP port ranges (i.e., 1 to 65535).
For Common Configuration, for Health Reporting, select None. App Connector health reporting must be set to None because each FTP data channel is pseudo-random and opened on a per client basis.
For Additional Configuration, from the Bypass drop-down menu, select Use Client Forwarding Policy. You need to create a client forwarding policy with the rule Forward to ZPA.
Complete the configuration for the new application.

blocks.text: Zscaler recommends that your users access a proper FTP client (i.e., FireFTP, FileZilla, CuteFTP, etc.). Command line FTP on Windows and macOS does not implement passive FTP correctly.
